claim: A European Journal of Immunology study reported that MIF and the MIF receptor CD74 were downregulated, while CXCR4 was upregulated, in B cells from early MS patients, and described reciprocal regulation among MIF, CD74, and CXCR4 in human B cells.
future_grounding_route: Use only as segregated MS B-cell MIF/CD74 context unless the project's held cell-state data are used to rerun B-cell MIF/CD74/CXCR4 scoring and compare it to the V26 coupled-axis loadings.
project_use: Sharper external context for the MIF-CD74 receptor-state side of the V26 coupled APC-axis architecture.
relationship_note: This source overlaps MS, B cells, MIF, CD74, and CXCR4, but it does not independently reproduce the project's cross-modality coupled HLA/IFN-APC plus MIF-CD74 architecture.

source.citation: Klasen et al. The macrophage migration inhibitory factor pathway in human B cells is tightly controlled and dysregulated in multiple sclerosis. European Journal of Immunology. 2018.
source.label: EJI MIF/CD74 pathway in human B cells and MS

source_terms.license_or_terms_label: PubMed bibliographic metadata and short paraphrase only
source_terms.reuse_notes: V50 stores bibliographic metadata and a short paraphrased claim only; do not redistribute article text or treat it as project-grounded evidence.

why_unverifiable: The project has not rerun the external publication's B-cell expression and functional analysis in the external layer.
